design_limits: both arms share one process in fixed A then B order, so the first arm absorbs one-time imports; the -58 MB at 130 parents is that artifact, not a saving
one draw per (arm, size), no interleaving
lifetime footprint and max_rss are process-lifetime high-water marks, so arm B's include arm A's peak by construction
at a prefix, arm A walks n parents while arm B scans the whole ledger files
ab_measurement.instrument: tracemalloc, restarted per arm; footprint recorded but not used as retention evidence

attribution.conclusion: the month's whole unit/parent graph is about 4.7 MB. Prepare holds about 4.8 GB. The graph is roughly a thousandth of it, so no ledger or streaming change can move the number that stopped the rebuild. The cost is about 155 MB per distinct build key, paid inside monthly_demand.prepare, which builds one archive runner per key and which BOTH paths call identically
attribution.question: is prepare's memory per daily unit, or per build key?
attribution.resolved_by: removing the demand layer entirely and measuring the unit/parent graph alone on the real 1,690-parent month
attribution.why_it_was_ambiguous: units and build keys grow together across prefixes of one month, so a per-unit fit and a per-build-key fit are collinear and both fit

claim_boundary: whether replacing the profile's materialising prepare with the existing streaming seam fixes the memory that stopped the approved rebuild. It rebuilds no profile and authorises nothing

gate.full_population_b_run: NOT RUN, deliberately. The brief permits it only if B is safely under the limits; measured at 650 parents B holds 2.30 GB and 7.36 GB footprint, projecting to about 4.8 GB at 30 build keys, so it is not

supersedes_readiness_of.why: production source changed in this round, so that readiness decision no longer describes the code that would run

what_the_change_is_still_worth: the profile can no longer materialise a month-sized parent graph, and a silent fallback is impossible rather than merely unlikely
prepare is 2.4x faster in this layer (0.218 s against 0.517 s)
the enumeration is now verified, versioned and bound into the evidence, and stale ledgers from other producer sources are refused
one definition of a ledger's contents instead of two
what_was_built: tools/profile_monthly_cost_ledger.py now prepares through IndependentDailyRunner.prepare_from_ledgers over a verified, versioned, append-only closure-ledger population, refuses to materialise above MATERIALISED_PARENT_LIMIT, re-verifies the ledgers it just wrote, binds them to the producer source manifest, and records the binding in the profile evidence. monthly_search's ledger_unit_records was made public so both producers share ONE definition of a ledger's contents
where_a_real_fix_would_go: monthly_demand.prepare builds and retains one ArchivedDemandSumoRunner per build key for the whole run. A fix would create them lazily and release each after its build key is priced - which the two-phase cost ledger already groups by - or prepare build keys in waves. Not attempted here: it is a separate change to production costing code and needs its own approval and its own evidence
